Hon'Ble Mr Justice M. A. Chowdhary, Judge (Judgment

The Appellant-National Insurance Company Limited, through the medium of the instant appeal filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act of 1988'), has challenged the Award dated 28th of June, 2018 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Pulwama in Claim Petition bearing National Insurance Company Ltd vs Amina on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132427141/
1 No. 29/ Claim titled 'Mst. Amina v. Ghulam Muhammad Mir & Ors.', whereby an amount of Rs. 14,80,000/-, along with simple interest @ 6 percent per annum from the date of institution of the Claim Petition till its final realization, was granted to the Claimant-Amina.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
02 . The impugned Award has been challenged by the Appellant- Insurance Company on many grounds, as projected in the memo of appeal, however, the learned Counsel for the Appellant-Insurance Company, during the course of arguments, has assailed the impugned Award with regard to the findings returned by the Tribunal on issue No.3, which reads as under:
"Whether the Respondent No.1 was not having valid and effective driving license at the time of occurrence, if so, what would be its effect on the claim petition?"

03. The Tribunal, while deciding the issues, returned a finding with regard to issue No.3 holding that the Respondent-Insurer/ Appellant herein had failed to prove issue No.3 on the ground that the driver once licensed continues to possess the ability to drive the vehicle, unless he has incurred a physical disability and that the Insurer had also failed to prove that the license of the Respondent-Driver was fake or that it had not been renewed as on the date of accident.

04. Mr N. A. Dendru, the learned Counsel appearing for the Appellant-Insurance Company, argued that the accident in this case had taken place on the 18th day of March, 2009, with reference to which the Claimant/ Respondent No.1 herein was granted compensation by the Tribunal.

It is further submitted that the Respondent-Driver, though was issued the driving license on 21st of August, 1972, which was valid upto 20th of August, 1995, however, there is no proof with regard to the renewal of the said license till 20th of March, 2009 when it was again renewed upto 19th of March, 2012.

The learned Counsel argued that as on the date of accident viz. 18th of March, 2009,
the driving license could not be stated to be valid to drive the vehicle for not having been renewed and that the Tribunal had fallen in error, so as to hold that the driving license of the Respondent-Driver was valid as on the date of accident.

He further submits that the Appellant, as Respondent-Insurer before the Tribunal, had discharged its obligation by examining one of its official namely, Gulzar Ahmad Wani, Legal Assistant and the Licensing Clerk from the office of RTO,
Kashmir, namely, Irshad Ahmad, as its witnesses, who had stated that there was no record with respect to the renewal of license as on the date of accident or even upto one month prior to the date of accident.

It is, accordingly, prayed that the instant appeal be allowed and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in respect of issue No.3 be set aside holding that the Respondent-Insurer/ Appellant herein, in view of contravention of insurance policy, was not liable to pay compensation to the Claimant/ Respondent No.1 herein, rather it was entitled to recover the paid amount of compensation from the registered owner of the offending vehicle.

05. Mr S. H. Thakur, the learned Counsel, representing the Respondent No.2 herein/ Driver of the offending vehicle, ex adverso, argued that the Appellant-Insurance Company, as Respondent-Insurer before the Tribunal, had miserably failed to prove issue No.3, onus of which National Insurance Company Ltd vs Amina on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132427141/
2 had been placed on it.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the Respondent- Driver had taken a plea in his statement that his license was burnt twice, once by the Counter Insurgents (Ikhwanees) and that the license had been renewed from the office of the Licensing Authority viz. RTO, Jammu w.e.f. 15th of March, 2006 till 14th of March, 2009.

The learned Counsel further argued that though the accident had taken place on 18th of March, 2006 and the license was due to be renewed after 14th of March,
2009, however, for a period of thirty (30) days, the license is deemed to be effective from such expiry as per second proviso to sub-section (2) of Section 14 of the Act of 1988 which provides that every driving license shall, notwithstanding its expiry under this sub-section, continue to be effective for a period of thirty (30) days from such expiry.

He, accordingly, submitted that on expiry of the renewal date of 14th of March, 2009, the driving license of the Respondent- Driver was deemed to be valid even upto 13th of April, 2009, thereby covering the date of accident viz. 18th of March,
2009.

The learned Counsel for the Respondent-Driver, in this regard, submits that he had placed on record a certificate issued from the office of RTO, Jammu by laying a motion during the pendency of this appeal.
06. Heard learned Counsel for the parties and perused the pleadings on record.
I have also gone through the scanned record of the Tribunal and the impugned Award.

07. Admittedly, the issue of renewal of the license of the Respondent-Driver by the office of RTO,
Jammu and the documentary proof to that effect had not been placed on record before the Tribunal,
which was best suited to hold an enquiry on the said issue, even by recording evidence for and against or to examine any official from the Licensing Authority viz. RTO, Jammu with regard to the claim of renewal of license upto 14th of March, 2009.

Under such circumstances and on a perusal of the record of the case as also the impugned Award passed by the learned Tribunal, this Court is of the considered opinion that the matter requires to be further inquired into as to whether the driving license of the Respondent-Driver, as claimed by him before this Court, had been renewed upto 14th of March, 2009, so as to be valid as on the date of accident viz. 18th of March, 2009 in view of second proviso to sub-section (2) of Section 08.

Viewed thus, the findings recorded by the Tribunal on issue No.3 are, accordingly, set aside and the case is remanded back to the Tribunal, with a direction to hold an enquiry with regard to issue No.3 by permitting the parties to lead evidence, for and against, so as to return a fresh finding on issue No.3.
The contesting parties, through their Counsel, are directed to appear before the Tribunal on 25th of February, 2025.

09. Having regard to the fact that the quantum of compensation, as awarded by the Tribunal, is not disputed in this appeal and the contest is with regard to liability of the Insurer-Insurance Company or that of the Insured-Driver, which will hinge upon the finding to be returned by the Tribunal on issue No.3, coupled with the fact that the amount of compensation has been already deposited by the Appellant-Insurance Company before this Court, 50% of which is stated by the learned Counsel for the Claimant/ Respondent No.1 herein to have been released, the balance 50% is also directed to be released in favour of the Claimant/ Respondent No.1 herein, of course, on proper identification and after deduction of Court fee.
